```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, knitr, patchwork, conflicted)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, dplyr::mutate, dplyr::summarise, here::here)

TAB <- here("outputs", "tables", "backdating")
FIG <- here("outputs", "figures", "backdating")
ONSET_MIN <- 2000L; ONSET_MAX <- 2017L          # = build_04_backdating.R
LT_MAG <- 200; LT_DUR <- 4; LT_PRE <- 100       # = build_04_backdating.R

f <- function(...) file.path(TAB, ...)
pending <- function(what) cat(sprintf("\n> **Pending:** %s\n\n", what))
first_existing <- function(paths) { p <- paths[file.exists(paths)]; if (length(p)) p[1] else NA_character_ }

# --- accuracy helpers (pixel- or point-weighted) ---
acc <- function(onset, truth, w = rep(1, length(truth))) {
  dated <- !is.na(onset); e <- (onset - truth)[dated]; wd <- w[dated]
  tibble(coverage = 100 * sum(wd) / sum(w),
         exact = 100 * sum(wd[e == 0]) / sum(wd),
         pm1   = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 1]) / sum(wd),
         pm2   = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 2]) / sum(wd),
         pm1_of_all = 100 * sum(wd[abs(e) <= 1]) / sum(w),
         mean_error = sum(wd * e) / sum(wd))
}
fmt_acc <- function(x) x |> mutate(across(c(coverage, exact, pm1, pm2, pm1_of_all), ~ round(.x, 1)),
                                   mean_error = round(mean_error, 2))
acc_cols <- c("dated (%)", "exact (%)", "±1 yr (%)", "±2 yr (%)", "±1 yr, share of all (%)", "mean error (yr)")
# Naming rule: "Barenblitt replica" = OUR implementation of their method; "Barenblitt et al." = their data.
mlab <- c(barenblitt = "Barenblitt replica (ours)", landtrendr = "LandTrendr", ccdc = "CCDC")

# --- embeddings ground-truth test: v2 (3 methods, dense + thinned) preferred over v1 (dense, 2 methods) ---
# *_ccdc = the 3-method run; *_e = the rule-e test (2 methods, read separately), never picked here
v2_path <- first_existing(c(list.files(TAB, "groundtruth_v2_bar_hull.*_ccdc\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
                            list.files(TAB, "groundtruth_v2_.*_ccdc\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)))
v1_path <- first_existing(f("validate_backdating_vs_classifier_groundtruth_bar_hull.csv"))
gt <- if (!is.na(v2_path)) {
  read_csv(v2_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    rename(any_of(c(barenblitt = "bar", landtrendr = "lt", ccdc = "cc"))) |>
    pivot_longer(any_of(c("barenblitt", "landtrendr", "ccdc")), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset")
} else if (!is.na(v1_path)) {
  read_csv(v1_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(imagery = "full") |>
    rename(barenblitt = onset_bar, landtrendr = onset_lt) |>
    pivot_longer(c(barenblitt, landtrendr), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset")
} else NULL
gt_src <- if (!is.na(v2_path)) basename(v2_path) else if (!is.na(v1_path)) basename(v1_path) else NA
gt_is_v1 <- is.na(v2_path) && !is.na(v1_path)
gt_score <- function(x) x |> group_by(method, imagery) |>
  reframe(acc(onset, first_detected_year, n_pixels)) |> fmt_acc()

# --- Barenblitt classifica comparison: all three methods on Barenblitt's own 2019 footprint ---
# (diag_04_method_fidelity.R). Their labels run one year earlier than ours, so
# classifica + 1 is the comparable year; that script's window runs to 2018 for this reason.
fid_path <- first_existing(f("validate_backdating_fidelity_3methods.csv"))

# --- rule e (deployed since 2026-11-17) vs the plain replica ---
# ef = embeddings test on the Barenblitt et al. hull with bar / e / f (f only used for the persistent-loss
# flag); fid_e = the classifica comparison with onset_bar vs onset_bar_e.
ef_path    <- first_existing(list.files(TAB, "groundtruth_v2_bar_hull.*_ef\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE))
fid_e_path <- first_existing(f("validate_backdating_fidelity_e.csv"))
elab <- c(bar = "Barenblitt replica, plain", e = "Barenblitt replica + rule e (deployed)")
LATER_MIN <- 2007L                               # = build_04_backdating.R
```

```{r summary-numbers, include=FALSE}
gt_persist <- if (!is.null(gt)) gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) else NULL
bar_dense  <- if (!is.null(gt_persist)) filter(gt_persist, method == "barenblitt", imagery == "full") else NULL
```

# Summary

**What this is.** We want to know when mining began on land that is mined today. The embeddings
classifier maps mining only from 2017 on. So we take every pixel mined in 2017 (confirmed: also mined
in 2018, see `diag_03_embedding_product_report`), look back
through the Landsat archive (1998-2018) for the year its vegetation was cleared, and impute that as
the pixel's conversion year ("onset"). Joined with the classifier's first confirmed detections from 2018, this
gives one onset series for 2000-2025, which feeds the panel.

```{r bottom-line, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(bar_dense)) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "- **Method:** the Barenblitt-replica NDVI method (Section 1), with years that have only one clear image filled in from ",
    "their neighbours (rule e, Section 1.3), dates every pixel mined by 2017 to an onset year, %d-%d. The validation ",
    "numbers in this summary are for the plain replica; rule e's gain is reported in Section 2.4.\n",
    "- **When imagery is good, it finds the right year:** %.0f%% of reliable pixels are dated within ±1 year of ",
    "the year the embeddings classifier first detects them, with no systematic offset (mean error %+.2f yr).\n"),
    ONSET_MIN, ONSET_MAX, bar_dense$pm1, bar_dense$mean_error))
} else pending("embeddings ground-truth test")
thin <- if (!is.null(gt_persist)) filter(gt_persist, method == "barenblitt", imagery == "thin") else NULL
if (!is.null(thin) && nrow(thin)) {
  cat(sprintf("- **With imagery thinned to pre-2013 sparsity:** %.0f%% within ±1 year (dated: %.0f%%).\n", thin$pm1, thin$coverage))
} else cat("- **With sparse, pre-2013-like imagery:** pending (thinning test).\n")
cat("- **Why this method:** it dates nearly every pixel, which the panel needs. LandTrendr is precise where it fires but",
    "dates only a minority of pixels, so it serves as a confidence flag (`lt_agree`). CCDC: see Sections 2.2 and 2.5.\n")
cat("- **Weak spots, flagged rather than removed:** sparse early years (fake one-year dips such as the 2002 pile-up,",
    "which rule e roughly halves), pixels already bare at the start, and 2008. The `persistent_loss` flag separates",
    "credible dates from shaky ones (Section 2.4).\n")
cat(sprintf("- **Two panel conventions:** onsets from %d (main), and \"no mining before %d\" (robustness; earlier onsets become a starting stock).\n",
            ONSET_MIN, LATER_MIN))
```

# 1. Methods

For every pixel the embeddings classifier maps as mined in 2017, we look back through the Landsat
archive (1998-2018) for the year its vegetation was cleared. We use the method of Barenblitt et al.
(2021), the only existing galamsey onset data, with one fix:

1. Keep each year's **greenest NDVI value**.
2. If a year has only **one clear image**, replace its value with an interpolation between the neighbouring years (**rule e**). A single hazy image would otherwise create a fake dip.
3. Smooth over **3 years** and take the year of the **largest drop** as the onset.

Every pixel gets a year. The main limitation is the imagery: before 2013 a pixel has only about 1-3
clear images a year, against about 10 from 2015, so early dates are less reliable. Two flags mark
this: **`persistent_loss`** (the drop lasts, it is not a one-year dip) and **`lt_agree`** (LandTrendr,
a standard change-detection algorithm, finds the same year).

Two example pixels, one clean loss and one gradual (the smoothing spreads a gradual loss over
several years, which is why accuracy is judged within ±1 year):

```{r mechanism-fig, out.width='100%', results='asis'}
# 2-panel figure from diag_04_backdating.R (no fallback to the old 10-panel ndvi_timeseries_examples.png)
p <- file.path(FIG, "ndvi_timeseries_method.png")
if (file.exists(p)) include_graphics(p) else pending("example-pixel figure (`diag_04_backdating.R`, run on the rule-e asset)")
```

## 1.1 The imagery: Landsat 1998-2018

All dating methods rely on the Landsat archive, and how much imagery it holds decides how well
they can work. Before 2013 a mined pixel has about 1-3 clear observations per year; from
2015 about 10. The satellites explain why. Landsat 5 was in orbit throughout, but recorded little
over West Africa in the 2000s. Landsat 7 lost its scan-line corrector in May 2003, so every later
scene has striped gaps. Only Landsat 8 (from 2013) brought full, regular coverage. Landsat 6 never
reached orbit (1993), and Landsat 9 (2021) is after our window.

```{r scene-cov, fig.height=4.2, fig.width=8}
sc <- read_csv(f("scene_coverage_anchor2017.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
# Year y is drawn from y - 0.5 to y + 0.5, so a date (decimal year d) sits at d - 0.5 on the same axis.
XL <- c(1997.5, 2018.5)
missions <- tribble(
  ~sensor,          ~status,                         ~from,   ~to,
  "Landsat 5 (TM)",   "operating (sparse over Ghana)", 1997.5, 2011.87 - 0.5,   # imaging ended Nov 2011
  "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "full scenes",                   1999.29 - 0.5, 2003.41 - 0.5,   # launched Apr 1999
  "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "scan-line gaps (SLC-off)",      2003.41 - 0.5, 2018.5,          # SLC failure 31 May 2003
  "Landsat 8 (OLI)",  "full scenes",                   2013.28 - 0.5, 2018.5           # data from Apr 2013
) |> mutate(sensor = factor(sensor, rev(c("Landsat 5 (TM)", "Landsat 7 (ETM+)", "Landsat 8 (OLI)"))))

p_sat <- ggplot(missions, aes(y = sensor)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = from, xend = to, yend = sensor, colour = status), linewidth = 5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`full scenes` = "#2a78d6", `scan-line gaps (SLC-off)` = "#eda100",
                                 `operating (sparse over Ghana)` = "#9ec5f4"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = XL, breaks = seq(2000, 2018, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Landsat satellites in our imagery window") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank())

p_obs <- ggplot(sc, aes(year, mean_n_obs)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8", width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = p10_n_obs), colour = "#D7301F", size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = XL, breaks = seq(2000, 2018, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "clear obs per pixel-year", title = "Clear observations per mined pixel",
       caption = "bars = mean, red dots = 10th percentile (pixels mined by 2017)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

p_sat / p_obs + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 2))
```

<details class="more">
<summary>Show more: alternative methods, the method step by step, rule e and the flags</summary>

**Why this method over the alternatives**

Dating a land-cover change from a satellite time series is a standard problem in earth observation,
and there are several ways to do it. We compare three: two widely used general-purpose
change-detection algorithms, **LandTrendr** and **CCDC**, and the method **Barenblitt et al. (2021)**
used to date galamsey in south-west Ghana. All three look for the break in a pixel's vegetation
record. They differ in how much imagery they need and in whether they always return a year.

- **LandTrendr** (Kennedy et al., 2010). Reduces each year to one value (here median NBR), fits a
  piecewise-linear trajectory through the years, and takes the start of the largest loss segment.
  The loss counts only if it passes size, duration and starting-vegetation thresholds (we use
  Barenblitt et al.'s: magnitude > 200, duration < 4 yr, pre-value > 100).
  *Needs:* about one clear observation per year. *Pro:* robust to noisy single observations, and
  tells abrupt clearing apart from slow decline. *Con:* the thresholds leave most pixels undated,
  because gradual or partial losses on already-degraded land fail them (Section 2).
- **CCDC** (Zhu & Woodcock, 2014). Uses every clear observation: it fits a seasonal model (harmonics
  plus trend) to each pixel and flags a break when consecutive observations stray from the model's
  prediction (settings as Barenblitt et al.: minimum 3 observations, chi-square 0.8). Onset = the
  break with the largest NDVI drop. *Needs:* dense imagery, several clear observations per year, to
  fit the seasonal cycle and confirm a break. *Pro:* uses all the data and dates breaks within the
  year. *Con:* too data-hungry for the early record. With recent imagery thinned to pre-2013
  density, the share of pixels it dates collapses (Section 2.2).
- **Barenblitt method** (Barenblitt et al., 2021). Takes each year's greenest NDVI value, smooths
  it over 3 years, and picks the year of the largest drop (details in 1.1).
  *Needs:* at least one clear observation in each of four consecutive years. *Pro:* dates nearly
  every pixel, it is simple, and it produced the only existing galamsey onset data, so ours is
  directly comparable. *Con:* there is no minimum loss, so it always picks a year, even where
  nothing much happened. It is sensitive to changes in how many observations a year has (the 2002
  pile-up, Section 3), and the smoothing spreads a sharp loss over neighbouring years.

We deploy the Barenblitt method with one fix for single-image years (rule e, Section 1.3) and keep
LandTrendr as a confidence flag (`lt_agree`); Section 2.5 sets out why. **Naming:** "Barenblitt replica" means our implementation of their method;
"Barenblitt et al." means their published data.

**1.2 The Barenblitt method in detail**

For every pixel mined by 2017 (in the embeddings classifier's 2017 mask, and confirmed by its 2018 mask):

1. Take every clear Landsat observation 1998-2018 and keep each year's **maximum NDVI**.
2. Smooth with a **3-year centred moving average**.
3. Compute the **year-on-year loss** in that average.
4. The year with the **largest loss** is the onset year.

There is no minimum size of loss: every pixel gets a year. A year can only be scored if the pixel has
clear observations in four consecutive years around it, so sparse early years limit which years
can win. A clean forest-to-bare step shows up as equal losses in three consecutive years (from the
smoothing). Our year label is the later one, which matches when the classifier first sees the mine
(Section 2). Barenblitt et al. label the same loss one year earlier. The example figure above shows
both cases: in the clean loss the largest bar is unambiguous; in the gradual loss the smoothing
spreads it over several bars. Weak cases follow in Section 3.

**1.3 The deployed version: rule e and the credibility flags**

Step 1 takes each year's greenest value. With several clear images a year, one hazy or cloudy image
does not matter. With only one, that image *is* the year's value, and if it is bad the pixel shows a
fake one-year dip that step 4 then picks as the onset. Before 2013 a pixel has on average 3.5 such
single-image years in 1998-2018; from 2013 almost none.

**Rule e** replaces the value of a single-image year by a linear interpolation between the nearest
years with at least two clear images on either side. No year is dropped (dropping them removed real
early onsets too and pushed every date later), and years with two or more images are untouched, so
post-2013 dating is unchanged. Section 2.4 scores it.

The deployed asset also carries flags that the panel can use (full list in the appendix):

- **`persistent_loss`** (0/1): the pixel has at least one candidate year whose loss lasts, i.e. the
  median annual maximum NDVI over the 3 years after it is at least 0.15 below the median over the
  3 years before. A dip that recovers fails. Imagery runs to 2020 for this check only, so 2015-2017
  onsets get a full 3-year window. It barely changes *which* year is picked, but it separates
  reliable dates from unreliable ones (Section 2.4).
- **`onset_from2007`** with **`loss_from2007_x1000`**: the same rule-e dating restricted to 2007-2017,
  for the "no mining before 2007" convention (2007 = start of Barenblitt et al.'s dated series). A
  tiny post-2007 loss means the pixel was probably mined before 2007 and belongs in the starting stock.
- **`bare_pre2007`**: median annual maximum NDVI in 2004-2006 below 0.4, i.e. already bare going into 2007.
- **`n_interp_years`**: how many years rule e filled in.

</details>

# 2. Does it find the right year?

Apart from checking pixels by hand in historical imagery (not done yet), there are two ways to
judge the methods, each with a caveat:

1. **Against the classifier's own 2018-2025 conversions** (2.1, 2.2). Pixels the embeddings
   classifier first maps as mined in 2018-2025 have a known conversion year, independent of
   vegetation indices. But that year is the classifier's first detection, not the true conversion
   year, and recent imagery is far denser than the early record. 2.2 therefore repeats the test
   with the imagery thinned to pre-2013 density.
2. **Against Barenblitt et al.'s published conversion years** (`classifica`, 2007-2017; 2.3). These
   cover the real historical imagery, but they come from the same NDVI method the Barenblitt
   replica copies, so the comparison is tilted in its favour.

## 2.1 Against the classifier's 2018-2025 conversions

**Test:** pixels that first appear as mined in the embeddings classifier's masks in 2018-2025
(and were not mined in 2017) get that first-detection year as a reference. Every method is then
run on 2016-2026 Landsat imagery for the same pixels. Only pixels that stay mined in every mask after
first detection are scored, since their reference year is the most reliable.

```{r gt-signed, fig.height=3.2, fig.width=8}
if (!is.null(gt)) {
  gt |> filter(persistent == 1, imagery == "full", !is.na(onset)) |>
    mutate(diff = pmax(pmin(onset - first_detected_year, 4), -4)) |>
    group_by(method, diff) |> summarise(px = sum(n_pixels), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(method) |> mutate(pct = 100 * px / sum(px)) |> ungroup() |> mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    ggplot(aes(diff, pct)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") + facet_wrap(~ method) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -4:4, labels = c("≤-4", -3:3, "≥4")) +
    labs(x = "method year minus first-detection year", y = "% of dated pixels") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r gt-dense, results='asis'}
if (is.null(gt)) pending("embeddings ground-truth test") else {
  gp <- filter(gt, persistent == 1, imagery == "full")
  cat(sprintf("<small>Script: `diag_04_groundtruth.R` · %s pixels (%.0f km²)%s</small>\n\n",
              format(round(sum(gp$n_pixels[gp$method == "barenblitt"])), big.mark = ","),
              sum(gp$n_pixels[gp$method == "barenblitt"]) * 900 / 1e6,
              if (gt_is_v1) " · LandTrendr here uses the **old** single-year gate (>100), not the deployed 200/4/100 version." else ""))
  cat('<details class="more"><summary>Show table</summary>\n\n')
  gt_score(gp) |> mutate(method = mlab[method]) |> select(method, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("method", acc_cols)) |> print()
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```

**Reading it:** a peak at 0 means the year label lines up with when the classifier first sees
the mine, so the backdated era (to 2017) and the embeddings era (2018 on) mean the same thing at
the seam. This is a **best case** for imagery: 2018-2025 has about 10 clear observations per pixel
per year, against 1-3 before 2013.

## 2.2 The same test with sparse imagery

The same test, with each pixel's 2016-2026 imagery randomly thinned to about 2.5 clear observations
per year, the pre-2013 average (some years end up with none, as in the early record). The gaps are
random, whereas real early gaps cluster in the wet season.

```{r gt-thin-bars, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
if (!is.null(gt) && "thin" %in% gt$imagery) {
  gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) |>
    select(method, imagery, `dated` = coverage, `dated and within ±1 yr` = pm1_of_all) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(method, imagery), names_to = "measure", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(method = factor(mlab[method], mlab),
           imagery = factor(imagery, c("full", "thin"), c("dense (2016-2026 as is)", "thinned to pre-2013 density"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(method, pct, fill = imagery)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(pct)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834"), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 105), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of all scored pixels") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}
```

```{r gt-thin, results='asis'}
if (is.null(gt) || !"thin" %in% gt$imagery) pending("thinning test (`diag_04_groundtruth.R` with `THIN_TARGET = 2.5`)") else {
  cat("<small>Script: `diag_04_groundtruth.R` (`THIN_TARGET = 2.5`)</small>\n\n")
  cat('<details class="more"><summary>Show table</summary>\n\n')
  gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) |> arrange(method, imagery) |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method], imagery = recode(imagery, full = "dense", thin = "thinned")) |>
    select(method, imagery, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("method", "imagery", acc_cols)) |> print()
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```

## 2.3 Against Barenblitt et al.'s conversion years

All three methods are run on the real historical imagery, on Barenblitt et al.'s own mapped
footprint, so every one of their points can be scored and differences in what counts as "mined"
don't enter. Their years are shifted +1 to match our label convention (Section 1.2). Part of the
Barenblitt replica's agreement is mechanical, since it copies the method behind these years, and
their years are not ground truth: they share the same imagery gaps and single-image artefacts.

```{r cls-signed, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
if (!is.na(fid_path)) {
  d <- read_csv(fid_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(truth = 2001L + as.integer(classifica)) |>
    pivot_longer(c(onset_bar, onset_lt, onset_cc), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset") |>
    mutate(method = recode(method, onset_bar = "barenblitt", onset_lt = "landtrendr", onset_cc = "ccdc"),
           onset = if_else(onset == 0, NA_real_, as.numeric(onset)))
  d |> filter(!is.na(onset)) |> mutate(diff = pmax(pmin(onset - truth, 4), -4)) |>
    count(method, diff) |> group_by(method) |> mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    ggplot(aes(diff, pct)) + geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") + facet_wrap(~ method) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -4:4, labels = c("≤-4", -3:3, "≥4")) +
    labs(x = "method year minus (Barenblitt et al. year + 1)", y = "% of dated points") + theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r cls-compare, results='asis'}
if (is.na(fid_path)) pending("three-method classifica comparison (`diag_04_method_fidelity.R`)") else {
  cat(sprintf("<small>Script: `diag_04_method_fidelity.R` · %s points on Barenblitt et al.'s 2019 footprint, 2007-2018 window</small>\n\n",
              format(nrow(d) / 3, big.mark = ",")))
  cat('<details class="more"><summary>Show table</summary>\n\n')
  d |> group_by(method) |> reframe(acc(onset, truth), points = n()) |> fmt_acc() |>
    mutate(method = mlab[method]) |>
    select(method, points, coverage:mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("method", "points", acc_cols)) |> print()
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```

## 2.4 Rule e and the persistent-loss flag

**Rule e** (Section 1.3) is judged only on the embeddings test, whose reference years do not come
from NDVI. With dense imagery it changes nothing, as intended. With imagery thinned to pre-2013
density it dates a few more pixels within ±1 year and fewer 4+ years too early (a fake early dip
picked as the onset). The gain is modest. It is not scored against Barenblitt et al.'s years: those
share the single-image artefacts that rule e removes, so agreement with them is not the goal.

```{r rule-e, results='asis'}
early4 <- function(onset, truth, w = rep(1, length(truth))) {
  dated <- !is.na(onset); 100 * sum(w[dated & onset - truth <= -4]) / sum(w[dated])
}
if (is.na(ef_path)) pending("rule e embeddings test (`diag_04_groundtruth.R`, `RULE_VARIANTS = c(\"e\",\"f\")`)") else {
  ef <- read_csv(ef_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(persistent == 1)
  cat("<small>Script: `diag_04_groundtruth.R` (`RULE_VARIANTS = c(\"e\",\"f\")`, Barenblitt et al. study area)</small>\n\n")
  cat('<details class="more"><summary>Show table</summary>\n\n')
  ef |> pivot_longer(c(bar, e), names_to = "method", values_to = "onset") |> group_by(imagery, method) |>
    reframe(acc(onset, first_detected_year, n_pixels), early = early4(onset, first_detected_year, n_pixels)) |>
    fmt_acc() |> mutate(early = round(early, 1), method = elab[method],
                        imagery = recode(imagery, full = "dense", thin = "thinned")) |>
    select(imagery, method, coverage, exact, pm1, pm2, early, mean_error) |>
    kable(col.names = c("imagery", "method", "dated (%)", "exact (%)", "±1 yr (%)", "±2 yr (%)", "≥4 yr early (%)", "mean error (yr)")) |> print()
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```

**The persistent-loss flag** marks which dates to trust. In the thinned test:

```{r persist-flag, results='asis'}
if (!is.na(ef_path)) {
  ef |> filter(imagery == "thin") |> mutate(grp = if_else(is.na(f), "no persistent loss", "persistent loss")) |>
    group_by(grp) |>
    summarise(share = sum(n_pixels), pm1 = acc(e, first_detected_year, n_pixels)$pm1,
              early = early4(e, first_detected_year, n_pixels), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(share = 100 * share / sum(share)) |>
    mutate(across(c(share, pm1, early), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
    kable(col.names = c("pixels", "share of pixels (%)", "within ±1 yr (%)", "≥4 yr early (%)")) |> print()
}
```

Pixels without a persistent loss are dated within ±1 year only about a third of the time. Requiring
persistence does not date the remaining pixels any better than rule e; its value is in separating
reliable from unreliable dates. Nationally the flag is 0 for about a third of pre-2011 onsets and
13% of 2011-2017 onsets (Section 3). The panel keeps these pixels and uses the flag for a robustness
check that drops them.

## 2.5 Which method, then?

The panel needs an onset year for nearly every mined pixel, so what counts is the share of **all**
pixels that are dated *and* dated within ±1 year, which combines coverage and accuracy:

```{r method-choice, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(gt)) {
  ch <- gt_score(filter(gt, persistent == 1)) |> select(method, imagery, pm1_of_all, coverage)
  g <- function(m, im, col) round(ch[[col]][ch$method == m & ch$imagery == im])
  has_thin <- "thin" %in% ch$imagery
  for (m in intersect(c("barenblitt", "landtrendr", "ccdc"), ch$method)) {
    cat(sprintf("- **%s:** %s%% with dense imagery%s.\n", mlab[[m]], g(m, "full", "pm1_of_all"),
                if (has_thin) sprintf(", %s%% thinned to pre-2013 density (dates %s%% of pixels)", g(m, "thin", "pm1_of_all"), g(m, "thin", "coverage")) else ""))
  }
  cat("\n")
}
```

The Barenblitt replica is the only method that holds up when imagery is as sparse as before 2013,
because it dates almost every pixel. LandTrendr is precise where it fires but leaves most pixels
undated, so it serves as a confidence flag (`lt_agree`). CCDC needs several clear images per year
and dates few pixels once the imagery is thinned. The replica also matches the method behind the
only existing galamsey onset data.

## 3.1 Our series against Barenblitt et al.'s data

```{r series-data}
cls <- if (file.exists(f("classifier_era_area_2017_2025.csv"))) read_csv(f("classifier_era_area_2017_2025.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) else NULL
# One continuous onset series per region: backdated 2000-2017 (undatable pixels added at 2017, they are
# in the 2017 mask) + classifier first detections 2018-2025.
onset_series <- function(reg) {
  if (is.null(osum) || is.null(cls)) return(NULL)
  o <- osum |> filter(region %in% reg)
  back <- o |> filter(onset_year > 0) |> group_by(year = onset_year) |>
    summarise(new_km2 = sum(n_pixels) * 900 / 1e6, .groups = "drop") |> mutate(source = "backdated (Barenblitt replica, Landsat)")
  und  <- tibble(year = ONSET_MAX, new_km2 = sum(o$n_pixels[o$onset_year == 0]) * 900 / 1e6, source = "undatable (in 2017 mask)")
  new  <- cls |> filter(region %in% reg, year > ONSET_MAX) |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(source = "classifier (first confirmed detection)")
  bind_rows(back, und, new) |> arrange(year)
}
ours_bh <- onset_series("bar_hull")
ours_gh <- onset_series(c("bar_hull", "outside"))
theirs  <- if (!is.null(bar_area)) bar_area |> transmute(year = bar_year + 1L, new_km2 = bar_km2) else NULL
```

```{r series-pending, results='asis'}
if (is.null(cls)) pending("classifier-era series (`diag_04_backdating.R`, Section 2c)")
```

Both series count **new** mining area per year inside Barenblitt et al.'s study area, from 2008 (their
first year, shifted +1 to our label convention) to 2018. Ours is the backdated product to 2017 and the
classifier's first detections in 2018. The levels differ because the footprints differ (ours: everything
the classifier maps as mined; theirs: their own map), so the shape over time is what to compare.

```{r series-vs-barenblitt, fig.height=3.4, fig.width=9}
if (!is.null(ours_bh) && !is.null(theirs)) {
  cmp <- bind_rows(
    ours_bh |> group_by(year) |> summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(series = "ours (Barenblitt replica + classifier)"),
    theirs |> mutate(series = "Barenblitt et al. data (+1 yr)")) |>
    filter(year >= 2008, year <= 2018) |>
    group_by(series) |> arrange(year) |> mutate(cum_km2 = cumsum(new_km2)) |> ungroup() |>
    pivot_longer(c(new_km2, cum_km2), names_to = "measure", values_to = "km2") |>
    mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("new_km2", "cum_km2"), c("new area per year", "cumulative since 2008")))
  ggplot(cmp, aes(year, km2, colour = series)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`ours (Barenblitt replica + classifier)` = "#2C7FB8", `Barenblitt et al. data (+1 yr)` = "#D7301F")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2008, 2018, 2)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "km²", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

```{r series-corr, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(ours_bh) && !is.null(theirs)) {
  j <- inner_join(ours_bh |> group_by(year) |> summarise(ours = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop"),
                  theirs |> rename(bar = new_km2), by = "year") |> filter(year >= 2008, year <= 2018)
  cat(sprintf("Correlation of new area per year, 2008-2018: r = %.2f.\n\n", cor(j$ours, j$bar)))
}
```

## 3.2 The full series, 2000-2025

The backdated product (to 2017) joined with the classifier's first confirmed detections (2018-2025).
From 2017 on, both are cleaned by the temporal rule (Rule B: a status counts only when two consecutive
years agree; see `diag_03_embedding_product_report`).

- **Bars:** new mining area per year, coloured by source.
- **Line:** the cumulative total of the bars, i.e. Option 1, "ever mined": a pixel stays mined once it
  has been mined. This is the panel's main spec.
- **White dots (2017-2025):** Option 2, "currently mined". The same rule, but a pixel can exit after two
  years in a row of "not mine". The gap between line and dots is land mined earlier that no longer
  shows as mined: revegetation, flooding or abandonment, not one-year flicker, which the rule removes.
- **2025** cannot be confirmed (no 2026 mask), so its bar is provisional.

Dashed lines mark 2007 (under the "no mining before 2007" convention, everything earlier becomes a
starting stock) and the 2017/2018 seam between backdating and the classifier.

```{r series-full, fig.height=6.5, fig.width=9}
if (!is.null(ours_gh)) {
  full <- bind_rows(ours_bh |> mutate(region = "Barenblitt et al. study area"), ours_gh |> mutate(region = "All of Ghana"))
  cumline <- full |> group_by(region, year) |> summarise(new_km2 = sum(new_km2), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(region) |> arrange(year) |> mutate(cum_km2 = cumsum(new_km2)) |> ungroup()
  stock <- bind_rows(cls |> filter(region == "bar_hull") |> mutate(region = "Barenblitt et al. study area"),
                     cls |> group_by(year) |> summarise(stock_km2 = sum(stock_km2), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(region = "All of Ghana")) |>
    select(region, year, stock_km2)
  sc_f <- max(cumline$cum_km2) / max(full$new_km2)   # second axis scale
  ggplot() +
    geom_col(data = full, aes(year, new_km2 * sc_f, fill = source), width = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = cumline, aes(year, cum_km2), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(data = stock, aes(year, stock_km2), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(LATER_MIN - 0.5, 2017.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    facet_wrap(~ region, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_y_continuous(name = "cumulative mined area (km², line)",
                       sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / sc_f, name = "new area per year (km², bars)")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`backdated (Barenblitt replica, Landsat)` = "#2C7FB8", `undatable (in 2017 mask)` = "grey60",
                                 `classifier (first confirmed detection)` = "#FDB863")) +
    labs(x = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 3.3 Why early dates are weaker

The confidence flags, grouped into three onset periods:

```{r results-flags-period}
if (!is.null(osum) && "persistent_loss" %in% names(osum)) {
  osum |> filter(onset_year > 0) |>
    mutate(period = cut(onset_year, c(ONSET_MIN - 1, LATER_MIN - 1, 2010, ONSET_MAX),
                        labels = c(sprintf("%d-%d", ONSET_MIN, LATER_MIN - 1), sprintf("%d-2010", LATER_MIN), sprintf("2011-%d", ONSET_MAX)))) |>
    group_by(period) |>
    summarise(share = 100 * sum(n_pixels) / sum(osum$n_pixels[osum$onset_year > 0]),
              persist = 100 * weighted.mean(persistent_loss == 1, n_pixels),
              lt_ag = 100 * weighted.mean(lt_agree == "agree", n_pixels),
              lt_dis = 100 * weighted.mean(lt_agree == "disagree", n_pixels),
              lt_none = 100 * weighted.mean(lt_agree == "no_signal", n_pixels),
              med_loss = matrixStats::weightedMedian(deriv_x1000, n_pixels),
              small = 100 * weighted.mean(deriv_x1000 < 50, n_pixels),
              bare = 100 * weighted.mean(start_class == "bare", n_pixels), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(across(-period, ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
    kable(col.names = c("onset period", "share of dated area (%)", "persistent loss (%)", "LandTrendr agrees (%)",
                        "LandTrendr disagrees (%)", "LandTrendr: no break (%)", "median loss (×1000)",
                        "loss <50 (%)", "bare in 1998-2002 (%)"),
          caption = "Confidence flags by onset period, all of Ghana (area-weighted).")
}
```

Early onsets (before 2011) are less reliable for five reasons:

1. **The loss persists less often.** About two thirds of early onsets show persistent loss, against 87% from 2011 on.
2. **LandTrendr rarely confirms them.** It seldom gives a different date. Mostly it finds no break that passes its own threshold, so early dates lack independent confirmation more than they face contradiction.
3. **The losses are smaller.** The median early loss is about 60% of the post-2011 median, and a quarter are below 50. A small loss is where noise or ordinary farm and cocoa clearing can win the steepest-loss pick, which is the source of the "dated ≥4 years early" errors in Section 2.
4. **More pixels were already bare in 1998-2002**, especially among 2007-2010 onsets. For these, the date is probably a later disturbance of an existing site, not the first mining.
5. **The design itself:** no test covers onsets before 2007. The classifier ground truth starts in 2018, and Barenblitt et al.'s dates start in 2007. Also, only pixels mined in 2017 are dated, so an early site has had 10-17 years to regrow and be disturbed again, which gives several candidate losses where a late site usually has one.

## 3.4 Weak spots, by example

Most weak spots trace back to the sparse early imagery (Section 1.1). Three example pixels: a one-year dip (a single low observation creates a false onset, the cause of
the 2002 pile-up), a pixel that was already bare at the start (no real loss to find), and a pixel
dated years before Barenblitt et al.'s year.

```{r weakspots-fig, out.width='100%', results='asis'}
p <- file.path(FIG, "ndvi_timeseries_weakspots.png")
if (file.exists(p)) include_graphics(p) else pending("weak-spots figure (`diag_04_backdating.R`, regenerated from the asset)")
```

| Weak spot | What we see | How it's handled |
|---|---|---|
| Already bare in 1998-2002 | 3.9% of dated area nationally; smaller losses; real onset may predate the series | flag `start_ndvi_x1000`; `bare_pre2007` sends such pixels to the starting stock under the "from 2007" convention |
| Few computable years | some pixels choose from only a handful of candidate years | flag `n_computable_years`, `n_obs_years` |
| 2002 pile-up | 7.4% of onsets with the plain replica (0.5% in 2001). A single-image artefact: 57% of 2002 pixels have only one clear image in 2003, the first Landsat 7 SLC-off year, against 17% of other pixels, and the median NDVI dips 0.81 → 0.44 → 0.76 (`notes/archive/diag_06_onset_2002_check.R`). The same one-year dips make up 40-60% of all onsets before 2012 | rule e (deployed): 2002 falls to about 4.2% of onsets, with half of the 2002 pixels moving, mostly to 2005 or later (`diag_06` sample); the rest keep a 2002 date and are flagged where the loss does not persist (`persistent_loss`). Nationally 2002 is still 4.6% of dated area, about 1.7× its neighbours. A likely cause: rule e only fixes years with exactly one image, so a 2003 with two or three images that are all low (dry-season-only dates, haze, partly masked cloud) still gives a dip. Before 2007, so it is in the starting stock under both conventions |
| 2008 (and 2009) | Still present with rule e: 2008 has 9.7 km², about half its neighbours, and 28% of it was already bare in 1998-2002 (2009: 18%; 2004-2007: 4-7%). With no real loss to find, the steepest-loss pick lands on a small fluctuation, and these land in 2008/09 more often than in other years. Cause not established: possibly noisy annual values in the Landsat 7 SLC-off years, when Landsat 5 recorded little over West Africa. An earlier check found Barenblitt et al.'s data often date these pixels much later (not yet re-run on the rule-e asset) | `persistent_loss` does not catch it (68%, normal). The bare-at-start flag does: under the "from 2007" convention, `bare_pre2007` sends such pixels to the starting stock |
| Smaller losses before 2011 | sparser imagery or more gradual early clearing | no minimum-loss threshold: it would cut early years far more and make mining look later |


# 4. Settings and why

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor footprint | embeddings mask, mined in 2017 and 2018 (Rule B) | one-off 2017 blips get no onset year; 2018+ onsets come from the classifier directly |
| Onset window | 2000-2017 | 2017 was cut off before (8.9% "undatable") |
| Imagery | 1998-2018, full year (to 2020 for the persistence check only) | the 3-yr average needs a year either side; shortening it would misdate early mining |
| Single-image years | interpolated from the nearest ≥2-image years (rule e) | removes fake one-year dips without dropping any year (Sections 1.3, 2.4) |
| Year label | later year of the loss | matches the classifier's first detection (Section 2) |
| Minimum loss | none | no natural cut-off; a threshold biases the timeline |
| Persistent loss | 3-yr median after ≥ 0.15 below 3-yr median before | flag only; separates credible from shaky dates |
| Later convention | onsets from 2007 | start of Barenblitt et al.'s dated series |
| LandTrendr (cross-check) | mag > 200, dur < 4, pre-value > 100 | Barenblitt et al.'s comparison settings |

# Appendix: deployed asset bands

`mine_onset_year_2000_2017_rulee`, 30 m (replaces `mine_onset_year_2000_2017_barenblitt`, which is kept).
It was built on the raw 2017 anchor. `diag_04_backdating.R` and `b_04` mask it to the confirmed anchor
(`cur_2017` of `mine_status_ghana_c4_ruleB_2017_2025`), which is equivalent to rebuilding it, since every
pixel is dated on its own.

| Band | Meaning | No-data value |
|---|---|---|
| `onset_year` | rule-e onset year, 2000-2017 | 0 = not datable |
| `ndvi_deriv_x1000` | size of the winning loss, ×1000 | -9999 |
| `onset_from2007` | rule-e onset restricted to 2007-2017 | 0 |
| `loss_from2007_x1000` | size of that loss, ×1000 | -9999 |
| `persistent_loss` | 1 = some loss persists 3 years (Section 1.3) | – |
| `reference_tier` | 0 = onset before 2007, 1 = 2007+ (comparable with Barenblitt et al.'s years) | 9 |
| `lt_agree` | 0 LandTrendr agrees ±2 yr, 1 disagrees, 2 no LandTrendr signal | 9 |
| `n_obs_years` | years 1998-2018 with ≥1 clear observation | – |
| `n_computable_years` | candidate years that could be scored | – |
| `n_interp_years` | years 1998-2018 filled in by rule e | – |
| `bare_pre2007` | 1 = median annual max NDVI 2004-2006 < 0.4 | 9 |
| `start_ndvi_x1000` | median rule-e annual max NDVI 1998-2002, ×1000 | -9999 |

Sources: CSVs and figures in `outputs/tables/backdating/` and `outputs/figures/backdating/`,
produced by `build_04_backdating.R`,
`diag_04_groundtruth.R`, `diag_04_method_fidelity.R` and
`diag_04_backdating.R`.
